summary: Client spell-preview data of a projectile spell being aimed: projectile counts and one ProjectilePathTargetData per target. Seen once, all zero, in the inventory scenario when a Fireball scroll was used (preview opened). Read by ecl::spell_preview::GetAimDirection (macOS) for targeting types 3/0xB.

fields.name: field_0
fields.evidence: Element of the array at ProjectilePathTargetData+0x40: the Windows array destroy/resize bg3.exe+0x70E230 works with stride 0x70. Members not read.

fields.name: field_0
fields.evidence: not touched by the Windows destructor; not read

fields.name: field_10
fields.evidence: Windows element destructor bg3.exe+0x709510 destroys +0x10 with the plain-key HashSet destructor bg3.exe+0x582AD0 (48 bytes: buckets, next ids, keys - what the first worker read in the Toolkit as three arrays at +0x10/+0x20/+0x30). Key width NOT established: uint64_t is a placeholder.

fields.name: field_40
fields.evidence: Windows element destructor bg3.exe+0x709510 resizes +0x40 to 0 with bg3.exe+0x70E230 (element stride 0x70) and frees its buffer.

fields.name: field_50
fields.evidence: not touched by the Windows destructor; macOS GetAimDirection reads 8 bytes at +0x74 when the bool at +0x80 is set (macOS offsets, hints only)

fields.name: field_98
fields.evidence: Windows element destructor bg3.exe+0x709510 calls the virtual destructor (slot 0, flag 1) of the object at +0x98 and clears it - an owned polymorphic object.

fields.name: field_0
fields.evidence: Windows: bg3.exe+0x1EE0230 walks the query DAT_1463543D4, which bg3.exe+0x1EF1930 registers as {ecl::spell_preview::ProjectilePathComponent (written), ecl::spell_cast::StateComponent}, with component stride 0x18 and stores max(1, n) at +0 (a projectile count from the spell, targeting types 3/0xB); adder bg3.exe+0x1EEB120 zeroes it. Live 0.

fields.name: field_4
fields.evidence: Windows: same function bg3.exe+0x1EE0230 stores the result of bg3.exe+0xFCEA40 (types 3/0xB) or max(1, n) (type 4) at +4. Live 0.

fields.name: Targets
fields.evidence: Windows: the component destructor bg3.exe+0x6BCAC0 (registered by the adder bg3.exe+0x1EEB120, size 0x18) resizes +8 to 0 with bg3.exe+0x6DEB10, which destroys elements with stride 0xA0 (bg3.exe+0x709510), and frees the buffer; macOS names the element ls::DynamicArray<ecl::spell_preview::ProjectilePathTargetData>.

open_questions: ProjectilePathTargetData (0xA0): only its containers are known on Windows (HashSet at +0x10 with an unknown key width, Array of 0x70-byte elements at +0x40, owned object at +0x98); +0..+0xF and +0x50..+0x97 are unread here.
The Toolkit-based first version had four arrays at +0x10/+0x20/+0x30/+0x40; the Windows destructor shows a 48-byte HashSet + one Array instead.
status_reason: only empty (all-zero) instances were seen: the member boundaries are untested
second_pass: Tied the counts at +0/+4 to this type through its query (registered by bg3.exe+0x1EF1930, written by bg3.exe+0x1EE0230) and read the Windows destructors bg3.exe+0x6BCAC0 / bg3.exe+0x6DEB10 / bg3.exe+0x709510: the element is 0xA0 bytes with a HashSet at +0x10, an Array of 0x70-byte elements at +0x40 and an owned object at +0x98. The component's own three members are settled; the element's contents are not.
